knowledge:
- key_parameters: ms1_data=Raw MS1 data extracted using RaMS::grabMSdata used for metric calculation and visualization ;; rt_window_width=Width of the retention time window used in pickyPCA (default 1) ;; ppm_window_width=Width of the ppm window used in pickyPCA (default 5) ;; likelihood_threshold=Probability threshold (0 to 1) in updateXcmsObjFeats and logModelFeatQuality above which features are classified as "Good" (default 0.5) ;; verbosity=Controls console output and plotting behavior in extractChromMetrics, pickyPCA, logModelFeatProb, logModelFeatQuality, and updateXcmsObjFeats
- alternatives: XCMS, MzMine, MSDIAL=Used for preliminary peak list extraction, peakpicking, retention time correction, or correspondence (squallms does not perform these itself) ;; Proteowizard's msconvert=Used to convert proprietary mass-spec formats to open-source mzML/mzXML formats required by squallms
- when_to_use: Appropriate when analyzing untargeted LC/GC-MS data where automated peakpicking algorithms (like XCMS) have high false-positive rates, and the user needs a robust, semi-labeled approach to filter out low-quality noise peaks before downstream analysis.
- pitfalls: Retention time bounds must be uncorrected. If corrected retention times are provided to extractChromMetrics, the data extracted from the mz(X)ML files will be incorrect ;; Large datasets may not fit into computer memory; users should subset the data (e.g., using only quality control files or pooled samples) for quality calculations ;; The PCA separation of good/bad peaks is not guaranteed to be consistently along the first or second PC, especially if there is a large biological signal present (recommends adjusting the number of PCs and clusters in the lasso tool)

workflows.name: semi_labeled_peak_filtering
workflows.intent: Filter out low-quality chromatographic features from an XCMS object using a semi-labeled logistic regression model trained on manual or lasso-labeled peak quality metrics.
input: mzML_files (raw mass spectrometry data files in mzML or mzXML format)
xcms_filled (an XCMS object containing filled chromatographic peaks)
workflows.stages: 1. Flatten the XCMS object to extract feature and peak bounding box information using makeXcmsObjFlat ;; 2. Extract raw MS1 data using RaMS::grabMSdata ;; 3. Calculate peak quality metrics (similarity to bell curve and signal-to-noise ratio) using extractChromMetrics ;; 4. Label a subset of features as "Good" or "Bad" using interactive manual labeling (labelFeatsManual) or PCA-based lasso labeling (labelFeatsLasso) ;; 5. Train a logistic regression model and predict quality probabilities for all features using logModelFeatProb and logModelFeatQuality ;; 6. Filter and update the original XCMS object to retain only high-quality peaks using updateXcmsObjFeats
workflows.code:
feat_peak_info <- makeXcmsObjFlat(xcms_filled) %>%
    select(feature, starts_with("mz"), starts_with("rt"), filename, filepath)

msdata <- grabMSdata(unique(feat_peak_info$filepath), verbosity = 0)

shape_metrics <- extractChromMetrics(feat_peak_info, ms1_data = msdata$MS1)

manual_classes <- labelFeatsManual(feat_peak_info, ms1_data = msdata$MS1)

lasso_classes <- labelFeatsLasso(feat_peak_info, ms1_data = msdata$MS1)

class_labels <- lasso_classes
class_labels[!is.na(manual_classes)] <- manual_classes[!is.na(manual_classes)]

pred_probs <- logModelFeatProb(shape_metrics, class_labels)

pred_classes <- logModelFeatQuality(shape_metrics, class_labels, verbosity = 1)

final_xcms <- updateXcmsObjFeats(xcms_filled, shape_metrics, class_labels,
    verbosity = 0, likelihood_threshold = 0.5
)
